extra.message: User-controlled input from the request body (sqli.get('username')) is interpolated directly into a SQL query string via an f-string and passed to cur.execute(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. ' OR '1'='1) to bypass authentication, read all user records, or exfiltrate data. Use parameterized queries instead.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: User-controlled input from the request body (ssti.get('mathexp')) is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and then rendered with test.render() on line 12. This allows Server-Side Template Injection, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary Python code (e.g. {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}) leading to remote code execution. Never build templates from untrusted input.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: User-controlled input from the request body (xss.get('username')) is reflected back in the response without any sanitization or output encoding. If rendered in an HTML context by a client, an attacker can inject script (reflected XSS). The endpoint returns attacker-controlled data verbatim.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: User-controlled input from the request body (rfi.get('imagelink')) is passed directly as the URL to requests.get() with no validation of scheme or host. An attacker can force the server to make arbitrary outbound requests to internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ cloud metadata, internal admin endpoints) or use file:// style schemes, resulting in Server-Side Request Forgery. The response body is also returned to the attacker.

User-controlled input from the request body (lfi.get('filename')) is passed unvalidated to fetchfile(), which calls open(name).read() on line 3. An attacker can supply a path such as ../../etc/passwd or an absolute path to read arbitrary files on the server filesystem (path traversal / local file inclusion). The file contents are returned in the response.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The fetchfile() helper opens a file using an unvalidated name argument (open(name).read()). When called from lfivuln() with attacker-controlled input, this enables arbitrary file read via path traversal. The function performs no path normalization or directory restriction.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The attacker-controlled HTTP Host header (headerss['Host']) is reflected unsanitized into an HTML anchor href in the response. This enables Host Header Injection / HTTP header poisoning attacks, such as poisoning password-reset links to point to an attacker-controlled domain, as well as reflected XSS via the href attribute since the value is not escaped.

cwe: CWE-644: Improper Neutralization of HTTP Headers for Scripting Syntax

extra.message: The raw database exception message is returned to the client in the HTTP response ({'msg': f'{e}'}). This leaks internal details (SQL error text, schema, query structure) that aid SQL injection exploitation and other attacks. Errors should be logged server-side and a generic message returned.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The Flask application is run with debug=True and bound to host 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces). Debug mode enables the Werkzeug interactive debugger, which allows arbitrary Python code execution via the debugger console (PIN can often be bypassed) and discloses stack traces with sensitive data. This must never be enabled in production.

The outbound requests.get() call sets verify=False, disabling TLS certificate validation. This exposes the server to man-in-the-middle attacks on the fetched resource, allowing interception or tampering of the request and response.

A user account is seeded into the database with hardcoded, trivially-guessable credentials (username 'admin' / password 'admin'). Default/weak hardcoded credentials allow trivial authentication bypass. A second hardcoded account (mike/kaines) is created on line 25.
